summary: Monstellar is a solo NASA Space Apps 2026 project that uses real SPHEREx infrared observations to help users explore astronomical data. It retrieves targeted sky images from NASA's data archives, processes FITS files, and presents the resulting observations through an accessible web interface, making infrared astronomy easier to explore and understand.
details:
Monstellar is an interactive, browser-based astronomy visualization platform developed for NASA Space Apps 2026, focusing on the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Its purpose is to make NASA's SPHEREx infrared observations easier to explore, understand, and investigate through an accessible and interactive interface.

The platform allows users to search for astronomical objects by entering their coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination) or object names. It retrieves real SPHEREx spectral image data from NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) and transforms the observations into an interactive visual experience. Users can explore multiple observation dates, compare images, inspect different infrared wavelengths, and examine spectral features associated with water, carbon dioxide, and carbon monoxide ice bands.

Monstellar includes several analytical and visualization features, including time-based image playback, image blinking, difference imaging, image stacking, spectral exploration, and astronomical source overlays using Gaia DR3 and AllWISE catalogues. It also provides wavelength measurements, image quality information, and variance data to help users investigate astronomical observations.

The project is built using browser-based web technologies, JavaScript, HTML, a Cloudflare Worker, and Node.js-based data processing tools. Its backend retrieves and processes astronomical FITS data, reducing unnecessary data while preserving important scientific information.

Monstellar aims to bridge the gap between complex astronomical datasets and accessible scientific exploration. By combining real NASA observations with interactive visualization and comparative analysis, it provides students, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers with a practical way to investigate infrared observations, examine potential moving objects, and better understand the dynamic nature of our universe.
